Not without one file. The tax file is the only dependency left, and I have been chasing it since Monday.
What happens if it does not arrive tomorrow?
If it does not arrive by Tuesday, I will have to push the review back to Wednesday morning. If it arrives today, we close on time.
Is there anything I can do from here?
Yes. Could you ask the tax team directly? A message from you moves faster than three from me. And if the BPO takes the postings, that frees up half a day on my side.
Done. So what can you commit to?
I can commit to Wednesday morning, not to Tuesday. I will keep you posted through the afternoon. And you — do you need the variance note at the same time, or can that follow?
Could you give me until Wednesday morning, and I will send you the completed reconciliation?
Unless it arrives by midday, I will have to push the review back.

One thing about chasing people, and it took me years to understand it. When you write to somebody because they are late, the sentence that works is almost never the one about them being late. It is the one about what happens next. Compare these two. You have not sent me the file yet. And: if you send me the file today, I can still close the account this month. The first one is about the past and about them. The second one is about the future and about the work, and it is the one that gets an answer, usually within the hour. I am not talking about being nice. I am talking about giving somebody a reason that is stronger than their own to-do list, because that is what they are choosing between when they read your message.

The hardest sentence for most people in my team is not the one where they ask for something. It is the one where they ask for more time. And what I notice is that they say it far too late, and then wrap it in three apologies, which makes it sound worse than it is. If you tell me on day two that you will need until Wednesday, that is planning, and I can move something. If you tell me on day five, at six in the evening, that is a problem, and now it is my problem too. So here is what I want. Tell me early, tell me exactly what you need, and tell me what I get in exchange. Could you give me until Wednesday morning, and I will send you the completed reconciliation with the variance note already written. One sentence, no apologies, and the answer is almost always yes.
